ai.description: *Altiphylax stoliczkai* reaches 50 mm SVL. It is grey-brown with dark dorsal crossbars and a pale venter. Key features include slender, clawed digits and granular dorsal scales lacking enlarged tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Altiphylax stoliczkai* is best distinguished by the presence of small, granular scales on its back, which lack the enlarged, keeled tubercles found in similar *Cyrtopodion* species.
ai.habitat: *Altiphylax stoliczkai* inhabits high-altitude arid regions of the Himalayas, typically found among rocky outcrops and scree slopes at elevations between 2,500 and 4,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Frontier Bow-fingered Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the rocky crevices of its arid, high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Altiphylax stoliczkai* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer summer months, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Altiphylax stoliczkai* occurs in the high-altitude trans-Himalayan regions of Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh, typically at elevations between 3,000 and 4,500 meters.
